doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

chapter: Cello group, family and the road
title: Bach, bossa nova and music becoming generic worldwide
summary: Classical favorites, bossa nova in Brazil then and now, and worry that world music is becoming generic.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: I’m curious, did you listen to a lot of Bach and Vivaldi as a child?

Um hum, yes. All through my life, Vivaldi is, and Bach, our favorite music. Because we listen to mostly classical music, and jazz. And not all jazz, and not all classical, but a bit of each. We also are totally enamored of the bossa nova that came in the 60’s, and we’ve been down to Brazil, and they don’t do that anymore.

Well they do it but rarely, you’d have to search for it. Now it used to be all over. The first time we went down there was in the 60’s, and boy you could just go to so many different clubs and hear the greatest music. But then when we went back a few years ago we went back and we worked down in São Paolo, and we were down there for a couple of weeks and it was hard to find good bossa nova. I’m sure it’s there, it’s like jazz.
You were in Brazil here.
Exactly.
Brazil now sounds like America in the tropics. You know that’s it.
Well everything is so generic all over the world now. You know you hear the same kind of — well I won’t say how I feel about it. But there’s some good music that you hear, but not enough.
Who did we hear on the awards, the western singer?
Oh yeah, oh God.
I remembered his name because I was so struck by this wonderful music. Great harmony. Great players.
I think Gill was his last name, I’m not sure.
His last name was Gill?
Maybe, yeah. Well anyway.
That’s as much as I can remember, but anyways it was excellent. It was just wow.
There are some good people in country music now.
Oh Vince Gill.
Vince Gill.
Vince Gill, yes.
Vince Gill and then that new young girl, Leann Rimes? She’s a fabulous singer, got a great voice and she’s just true blue, you know right in there. It’s the kind of stuff you like to hear.

Well it’s curious you say that things are becoming too generic. I mean world music is now a category you can go to the record stores and see world music. I guess I had a question there I’m not sure what it was. Except that—
I’ve got the answer if you can think of the question.

Okay I’ll try. There’s so much recording going on and everybody’s hearing everything from everywhere else, maybe it tends to dilute it some by the time everybody hears it and puts out their own version of it.
